newsitem.title: UK: NWE gasoline holds gains as cargoes leave Europe.
newsitem.headline: NWE gasoline holds gains as cargoes leave Europe.

text.p: NWE gasoline ended modestly higher on Wednesday as traders counted up the cargoes leaving Europe for the U.S. and Latin America.
An open arbitrage to the U.S. has fuelled fresh trans-Atlantic deals and supported NWE gasoline, traders said.
A broker said he counted up a total of 750,000 tonnes or 20 cargoes moving from Europe to the U.S. this month.
A Med trader said 250,000 tonnes was fixed at the end of this month out of the Med and NWE for the U.S. and to a lesser extent Colombia.

Traders said the heightened arbitrage interest was due to firm U.S. prices and ample European supply, and not necessarily from a flow out of the U.K. after the government, as expected, announced a three pence per litre tax increase on petrol as of Tuesday night.
The blockade by French truckers and a 24-hour strike by Elf workers was not having a significant impact on prices, traders said.
More exports out of France due to lower local demand may hurt prices, mostly in the Med, but longer-term a cut in output would support gasoline, they said.

"It is being overshadowed somewhat by the big build-up in inventories in the U.K. in the last two months because of the tax change and the fact the big differential between U.S. and U.K. prices is beginning to mop up some of those supplies," said Peter Bogin at Cambridge Energy Research Associates in Paris.
A 60,000 tonne cargo was confirmed sold on Tuesday out of a U.K. refinery and into the U.S. to meet its commitments, but the volume and price were not known.
At least two other cargoes were fixed this week as well, said a trader at a U.K. refinery.
Eurograde barges last traded at $212 for Rotterdam running refinery material. Barges rose about $4 on Wednesday to $211/$213 fob ARA.
Regular unleaded deals were scarcer with prices up $1 at $201/$203.
Premium unleaded cargoes were assessed up $2 at $225/$227 cif.
